description:
Disclaimer: the description of the nature and scope of the services and supplies of the Space Traffic Coordination Platform procurement is only indicative, aimed at outlining the concept in broad terms and it may need substantial adjustments. Therefore it shall not be considered final nor binding. The EU Platform for Space Traffic Coordination aims to address the exponential increase in active satellites and the associated risks of orbital collisions, including those posed by large constellations. The initiative seeks to structure, secure and expand coordination between satellite operators, public entities and commercial SSA providers, building on existing services developed under EU Space Surveillance and Tracking (EU SST). It is intended to extend coordination beyond current EU SST members by enabling the collection and processing of key information, such as contact details and manoeuvre data from non-registered or international actors.

The proposed platform should facilitate the secure, real-time exchange of operational data and ensure interoperability between the different actors involved in space traffic activities. The action should include the implementation of a sandbox to test and assess the “rules of the road”, providing a controlled environment to evaluate their practical application and support validation prior to broader implementation. In addition, the initiative will include engagement and awareness-raising activities aimed at identifying the needs and expectations of EU Member States, satellite operators and SSA providers (public and private).

Riigihanke esemeks on Starlink satelliitsandmeside teenuse (edaspidi Teenus) tellimine. Riigihanke eesmärk on sõlmida Teenuse tellimiseks ühe pakkujaga raamleping, mis kehtib 36 kuud alates lepingu sõlmimisest.

Riigihanke eeldatav maksumus on 600 000 eurot käibemaksuta ja raamlepingu maksimaalne maksumus on 1 000 000 eurot käibemaksuta.

Riigihanke eseme täpsem kirjeldus on toodud dokumendis „Lisa 1. Tehniline kirjeldus“ (sisaldab mh tellitavate teenuste loetelu ja teenuste osutamise nõudeid). / Kõrvaldamise alused ja kvalifitseerimistingimused: Vaata hanke alusdokumentidest

description-proc.eng: The object of this procurement is the delivery of satellite orthomosaic images to the National Land Survey of Finland ("NLS") . The production areas to be ordered are based on the national laser scanning and aerial imaging programme. The procurement includes the delivery of 10 production areas (3 priority 1 production areas and 7 priority 2 production areas) which are defined in more detail in Appendix 1 Technical requirements and Appendix 1.1 Production areas. This procurement forms part of the NLS' preparedness for the situation where aerial images cannot be obtained from all production areas due to GNSS interference. Therefore, the procurement also includes the possibility to order maximum of 5 additional production areas (priority 3 production areas). The production areas from which these priority 3 production areas are selected are indicated in Section 4 of the Appendix 1. NLS does not commit to purchasing any priority 3 production areas from the supplier under this procurement. If NLS orders priority 3 production areas, the supplier shall have the right to refuse to accept such orders. The object of the procurement and the production areas are described in more detail in Appendix 1 and Appendix 1.1. See also chapters 10 and 11 of the Appendix A Contract. TERM OF THE CONTRACT The contract enters into force upon signature. The objective is that the contract will be signed by the end of February 2027. Contract covers the needs for satellite orthoimages for 2027. However, the contract shall enter into force no earlier than when there is no impediment to its implementation within the meaning of the public procurement legislation, such as a prohibition on enforcement. The contract shall terminate without separate notice once the supplier has delivered all products ordered by the NLS and both parties have fulfilled all their obligations under the contract. The provisions concerning termination of the contract are set out in chapter 22 of the Appendix A Contract.
